resources.string: Ballooner is a simple app for creating short comics with images from your device.
Thank you so much for your support! ☕
Ballooner processes your selected images and comic text on your device. Images are copied to app-private storage for editing. The app does not collect, store remotely, or share personal data.
Ballooner is provided as-is for personal creative use. You are responsible for the images and text you add and for ensuring that your comics comply with applicable laws and third-party rights.

Choose how the page is divided into panels.
• Tap a card to open the options of that preset: Single, Strip, Grid or Custom.
• The card marked ACTIVE is the preset your comic uses now.
• Next opens the options of the active preset. Nothing changes until you open a preset.

Choose the shape of the single panel that fills the page.
• The shape tiles (Square, Classic, Custom, Auto) set the shape of the panels. Classic can be turned on its side with its rotate button, Custom has two sliders for Width and Height, and Auto follows the first image you add.
• The preview shows the panel as it will really be. Pinch, drag and twist the image to look around: this only looks, because images are placed in the next step.
• The corner-brackets button at the top left of the preview gives it the whole screen and gives it back; a double tap on the strip beside it does the same.
• The gear at the top right of the preview opens Comic style, which sets the border and corners of the page.
• Back returns to the preset picker and throws away what you changed here. Next keeps it and moves on to Images. Undo reverses the latest change.

Lay the panels out in a row or a column.
• Orientation chooses between across and down, and the Panels stepper (− and +) sets how many panels there are, from 2.
• The shape tiles (Square, Classic, Custom, Auto) set the shape of the panels. Classic can be turned on its side with its rotate button, Custom has two sliders for Width and Height, and Auto follows the first image you add.
• Drag the grip between two panels in the preview to take size from one and give it to the other. Choosing a shape tile puts every panel back to one size.
• Tap a panel in the preview to select it, and tap again to let go. The gear at the top right then styles only the selected panels; with none or all selected it styles the whole comic.
• The corner-brackets button at the top left of the preview gives it the whole screen and gives it back; a double tap on the strip beside it does the same. While the preview fills the screen, the round button at its bottom right lays the page on its side.
• Back returns to the preset picker and throws away what you changed here. Next keeps it and moves on to Images. Undo reverses the latest change.

Divide the page into rows and columns.
• The Rows and Columns steppers (− and +) set the size of the grid, from 2 each.
• The shape tiles (Square, Classic, Custom, Auto) set the shape of the panels. Classic can be turned on its side with its rotate button, Custom has two sliders for Width and Height, and Auto follows the first image you add.
• Tap cells in the preview to select them. Merge joins the selected cells into one larger panel and Unmerge splits it again; they float over the preview when the selection allows.
• Drag a grip to resize rows or columns. The padlock beside a row lets that row divide its own width; closing it puts the row back on the grid. Choosing a shape tile puts every panel back to one size.
• The gear at the top right of the preview styles only the selected cells, or the whole comic when none or all are selected.
• The corner-brackets button at the top left of the preview gives it the whole screen and gives it back; a double tap on the strip beside it does the same. While the preview fills the screen, the round button at its bottom right lays the page on its side.
• Back returns to the preset picker and throws away what you changed here. Next keeps it and moves on to Images. Undo reverses the latest change.

Draw your own layout by cutting the page.
• Drag across a panel in the preview to cut it in two.
• Every cut has a round handle at each end. Drag a handle to swing the cut, and drag both handles off the page to remove it.
• The shape tiles (Square, Classic, Custom, Auto) set the shape of the panels. Classic can be turned on its side with its rotate button, Custom has two sliders for Width and Height, and Auto follows the first image you add.
• Tap a panel in the preview to select it, and tap again to let go. The gear at the top right then styles only the selected panels; with none or all selected it styles the whole comic.
• The corner-brackets button at the top left of the preview gives it the whole screen and gives it back; a double tap on the strip beside it does the same.
• Back returns to the preset picker and throws away what you changed here. Next keeps it and moves on to Images. Undo reverses the latest change.

Put an image in each panel and frame it.
• Tap a panel to select it. An empty panel offers Add image, which opens your photos; pick several at once to fill the empty panels that follow.
• A filled panel offers Expand panel, which brings it up close, and Remove image. While a panel is expanded, Show the whole page goes back, the arrows at its bottom corners move to the previous or next panel, and the eye button hides or shows these handles.
• Pinch to zoom, drag to move and twist to turn the image inside its panel. It always covers the panel.
• Press and hold a panel, then drop it on another to swap their images. A double tap adds an image to an empty panel, or expands and collapses a filled one.
• Back returns to the preset options, Next moves on to Balloons, and Undo reverses the latest change.

Add balloons and write in them.
• The row of balloon buttons adds a Speak, Think, Whisper, Yell or Caption balloon to the selected panel. Tap a bare panel to choose which panel the next balloon goes in.
• Tap a balloon to select it, then type straight into it. A selected balloon has round handles: Move (top middle), Resize (bottom right), Balloon style (top left, for font, size and border) and Delete (top right). Drag the dots at its tail to aim and widen the tail.
• The button at the right end of the row sets whether the balloon belongs to its panel and is cut off at its edge, or hangs free over the whole page.
• The Expand panel handle brings a panel up close, and its arrows move between panels.
• Back returns to Images. Save writes the comic to your library and Share sends it as a PNG. Undo reverses the latest change.
